source.title: Non-Convex Optimization with Spectral Radius Regularization
source.authors: Adam Sandler; D. Klabjan; Yuan Luo

record.tranche_reason: Varies batch size and reports held-out accuracy after a fixed maximum of 100 epochs, conceptually testing V5. Its shifted and augmented test results are out of distribution and are not mapped to the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Only the USPS held-out test accuracy rows map to V5. Forest cover-type data are not image or language benchmarks. Shifted, augmented, transfer, and GAN results are out of distribution; spectral-radius results do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness.
record.test_reason: Table 5 tests batch-size effects on held-out image-classification accuracy in a new setting: a USPS CNN trained with Adam and spectral-radius regularization. A common maximum of 100 epochs is reported, but equal actual training durations are not established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the batch-size subsection but omits the paper's main conclusion: the authors claim their spectral-radius regularization improves robustness and transfer performance over baselines. They emphasize dataset-dependent tuning and report that excessive regularization collapses predictions to the majority class. Their batch-size experiments favor batch 128 overall despite smaller batches having larger spectral radii.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies batch size and measures held-out accuracy, but focuses on spectral-radius regularization and tests including distribution shifts rather than the generalization-gap setup in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes held-out accuracy; batch size also changes spectral radius.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller training batches produce larger Hessian spectral radii in the regularized forest and USPS models; Table 4 also shows that the batch used to compute the radius changes its value for a fixed trained model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian spectral radius depends on training batch size and on the batch used for its measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 70 USPS models, larger Hessian spectral radii track larger losses of accuracy from ordinary to augmented test images.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian spectral radius correlates with sensitivity to image corruption in this USPS setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Forest cover-type batch-size results concern tabular classification; the other robustness and transfer comparisons concern distribution shifts and spectral-radius regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size and spectral-radius regularization affect tabular accuracy and robustness to distribution shifts.

record.problems: The USPS held-out accuracy values are reported without uncertainty estimates. The text gives a maximum of 100 epochs but does not specify whether each batch-size run used the same number of epochs.
record.rows_left_out: Out-of-distribution augmented USPS accuracies and shifted forest cover-type accuracies are not rows for the in-distribution claim. Spectral-radius measurements do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning budgets.
Equal actual epoch counts are not established. Language models, longer-training remedies, learning-rate scaling with warmup, and controlled normalization or regularization adaptations are not tested.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, training-to-test gaps at comparable training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The numerical Table 5 accuracies are correctly extracted. Nonmonotonic accuracy across batches does not itself limit V5, which allows a workload-dependent threshold. The text's description of prior work in Section 5.3 conflicts with its own Section 2; use the reported results rather than that description. No supplied original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization are not tested.
Network width and test error across widths are not tested.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture is not compared for in-distribution generalization.
Adaptive optimizers are not compared with SGD for in-distribution held-out performance.
Language models, batch sizes beyond a workload-dependent threshold, and recipe adaptations are not tested. The reported out-of-distribution comparisons are excluded.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation tolerance and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures are not tested.
Removing memorized examples is not tested.

rows.subject: USPS convolutional neural network
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch size 32; maximum of 100 epochs.
rows.note: Lower than the batch-128 result, but higher than batch sizes 64, 256, and 512.
rows.check: This is a small-batch reference, not evidence of a large-batch penalty by itself. Its accuracy is 93.27%, below every other listed batch size; the note incorrectly places it above batches 64, 256 and 512. Add Adam, learning rate 0.001, and spectral-radius regularization with mu=0.005, K=0 to the conditions.

rows.subject: USPS convolutional neural network
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch size 64; maximum of 100 epochs.
rows.note: Lower than batch 128 and higher than batches 32, 256, and 512.
rows.check: This is a reference below the best-performing batch size, not a demonstrated large-batch penalty. Its 94.47% accuracy is below batch 512's 94.97%, contrary to the note. Add the regularized Adam recipe specified for R1.

rows.subject: USPS convolutional neural network
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch size 128; maximum of 100 epochs.
rows.note: Highest held-out test accuracy among the listed batch sizes.
rows.check: The 95.91% accuracy at batch 128 supplies the comparison baseline; highest accuracy does not itself establish V5's penalty. Add the regularized Adam recipe specified for R1.

rows.subject: USPS convolutional neural network
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch size 256; maximum of 100 epochs.
rows.note: Lower than batch 128 and higher than batch 512.
rows.check: Against batch 128's 95.91%, batch 256 reaches 94.42%, a 1.49 percentage-point decrease. The note incorrectly says it exceeds batch 512. Add the regularized Adam recipe; equal actual epoch counts and uncertainty are unreported.

rows.subject: USPS convolutional neural network
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch size 512; maximum of 100 epochs.
rows.note: Lower than batch 128, but the study does not report a monotonic decline with increasing batch size.
rows.check: Against batch 128's 95.91%, batch 512 reaches 94.97%, a 0.94 percentage-point decrease. V5 does not require a monotonic decline at every batch-size increment. Add the regularized Adam recipe; equal actual epoch counts and uncertainty are unreported.

relationships.condition: USPS CNN with spectral-radius regularization, batches 256 and 512 versus 128, under the reported common maximum of 100 epochs
relationships.reason: R4 and R5 fall to 94.42% and 94.97% from R3's 95.91%; this supports a penalty above batch 128, with equal actual epochs and statistical uncertainty unresolved.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy was lower above batch 128, but the comparisons, whether actual epochs were equal, and statistical uncertainty remain unresolved.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: USPS held-out test accuracy across batch sizes
reader_labels.reason: Batch 128 had the highest accuracy, but larger batches did not show a consistent decline: batch 512 exceeded batches 64 and 256 (R1–R5). The study reports a maximum epoch budget, not evidence that all runs used the same number of epochs.
